Below is a draft essay. Revise it so that it reads as if a US grade 8 student wrote it in class for a timed writing test. Keep the position it argues and keep it at about 237 words. The file must contain only the revised essay.

A measurement tool scored the draft on how it carries feeling. For each measure below it gives the current value and a target. Revise the essay so that its measures move to the targets; the tool will score the result again.
- positive charge (hedons per 1,000 words): now 90.7, target 110.2. Counts positive words such as good, love, fun.
- negative charge (dolors per 1,000 words): now 3.9, target 28.8. Counts negative words such as bad, hate, problem.
- words that carry charge (% of words): now 24.9, target 36.3. Counts share of all words that carry any feeling.
- charge under a negation (% of charge): now 6.7, target 0.5. Counts feeling words placed under not, never or n't.
- charge after an intensifier such as 'very' (% of charge): now 0.0, target 1.8. Counts feeling words placed right after very, really or so.
- charge after a contrast word such as 'but' (% of charge): now 0.0, target 0.0. Counts feeling words placed after but or however in the same sentence.
- net charge of the last fifth minus the text's mean (per 1,000 words): now 36.9, target -5.7. Counts how much more positive the last fifth is than the essay as a whole; negative means a more downbeat ending.

Draft:

Dear Principal Morris,

I heard you are deciding whether every student should have to do community service. I think you should require it, but keep the number of hours small, maybe ten a semester.

My friend Dana tutors second graders at Lincoln Elementary on Tuesdays. She started because her church group asked her to, and she complained about it for a month. Now she talks about a boy named Marcus who could not read a full page in September and finished a chapter book in March. She would never have met him if someone had not pushed her to sign up. A lot of us are like that. We don't volunteer because nobody asks, and then we assume we wouldn't like it.

I know the argument on the other side. Some of my friends work after school or watch their little brothers and sisters, and they say they have no time left. That is a fair point, which is why the requirement should be small and flexible. Ten hours is one Saturday morning a month. Students could also count things they already do, like coaching a youth soccer team or helping at a food pantry.

The park behind our school is covered in litter, and nobody cleans it. If each student gave a few hours, it would look different by spring. Please make service a requirement, and let us choose how we do it.

Sincerely,
A student
